classification.difficultyReason: Interpret brackets and combine union and intersection to shade two compound regions in three-set Venn diagrams.

spec.description: Three overlapping circles in a rectangular universal-set boundary; A upper left, B upper right and C below. The student diagram is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: Shade the union of C with the intersection of A and B.
spec.answerVisibility: Source pale-blue answer shading is reserved for the solution diagram.

answer.short: Shade all of $C$ and all of $A\cap B$.
answer.worked: $A\cap B$ is the overlap of $A$ and $B$. Its union with $C$ includes that overlap and every region inside $C$, including the triple intersection.

spec.description: Complete solution figure with all of C and the A–B overlap shaded light blue.
spec.mathematics: Shaded region is (A intersection B) union C.

spec.description: Three overlapping circles in a rectangular universal-set boundary; A upper left, B upper right and C below. The student diagram is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: Shade the part of A lying in B or C.
spec.answerVisibility: Source pale-blue answer shading is reserved for the solution diagram.

answer.short: Shade $A\cap B$ and $A\cap C$, including the triple intersection.
answer.worked: $B\cup C$ contains everything in $B$ or $C$. Intersecting this with $A$ keeps only the portions inside $A$: the overlap with $B$ and the overlap with $C$, including the triple intersection.

spec.description: Complete solution figure with the portions of A overlapping B or C shaded light blue, including the triple intersection.
spec.mathematics: Shaded region is A intersection (B union C).
